answer.rationale: Incumbent has refused price reduction, so renewing or renegotiating this cycle is a dead end under the 18% cut mandate. The primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, so I cannot defer the decision safely. The line is running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, so a large disruptive switch is risky — but memory_c2 documents a prior low-cost primary switch that cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing. Memory_c6 is relevant context for negotiating terms only and adds little now that the incumbent is out. I will verify c2 to confirm the prior low-cost switch was reliable end-to-end (not just on invoice accuracy), and verify c6 only to rule out any binding commitment that constrains this decision. With budget pressure forcing the primary lever, switching primary to the previously validated low-cost vendor is the only path that hits the 18% cut without raising delivery risk — provided onboarding speed and invoicing reliability from c2 hold. To respect the no-buffer constraint, I would scope the switch as a small guarded test rather than a full-volume cutover in this same cycle.
